pages.text: Up, up, up! Milo the mountain stretches high into the sky, taller than hills and trees below.
At the bottom, grass grows and animals walk. Higher up, the land becomes rocky and steep.
Near the top, the air feels colder. Some mountains wear snowy caps even in warm seasons.
Tiny streams begin to trickle down Milo’s sides. These streams can grow into rivers.
The water flows downhill, joining other streams, moving toward valleys and land below.
Some animals live on mountains. Goats climb rocky paths using strong legs and balance.
People also live near mountains. They hike, farm, and use mountain water to help grow food.
From the top, Milo can see far and wide. Mountains give us big views of the land.
Mountains change the weather too. Clouds can gather and bring rain or snow.
At bedtime, we remember: mountains are tall, cold at the top, and help give us rivers.
